title: Three pillars, three evidence families
caption: Environmental shifts produce statistical evidence, input-level attacks produce adversarial evidence, and system-level faults corrupt the machinery that produces both. The evaluation matrix needs one row per pillar plus a per-request competence row, because a passed test in one row proves nothing about another.
alt: Three columns for environmental shifts, input-level attacks and system-level faults, each with its evidence family and first defense

title: The risk-coverage curve is the serving contract
caption: Raising the acceptance threshold moves along the curve: lower accepted risk at lower coverage, but only when the score orders requests by error well. The rejected tail prices the fallback path in queue and reviewer capacity.
alt: Curve of selective risk against coverage with a threshold point and rejected-traffic fallback arrow

title: A fired metric is not a retraining command
caption: The three-level framework: calibrated alerts automate detection only; performance correlation splits investigation into three cases; the decision rules pick among update, investigate-first and continue-monitoring. Statistical significance alone never commands a weight update.
alt: Flow from drift alert through performance correlation to three decision outcomes

title: Three signals separate the masquerade
caption: The same symptom, falling accuracy with green health, can come from any pillar. Timing against deployment boundaries, reproducibility under fixed-input replay, and cross-layer correlation with infrastructure telemetry separate a software fault from drift or attack before choosing the intervention.
alt: Three diagnostic lenses converging on a falling-accuracy symptom: timing, replay and telemetry correlation
